newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RICHTER HAS HIGH HOPES FOR LEG-SORE DRUG.
newsitem.headline: RICHTER HAS HIGH HOPES FOR LEG-SORE DRUG.

text.p: Hungarian pharmaceutical company Richter Gedeon Rt said on Wednesday it expects strong sales for a new drug to treat leg ulcers, bed sores and wounds.

"Richter believes this product will be a success on the market and it will be profitable but I can't disclose information about the amount," Istvan Greiner, head of Richter's research and development department, told a news conference.
The drug, Curiosin, is the result of Richter's own research and development work for which the company planned to increase spending to 2.3 billion forints in 1996 from 1.7 billion in 1995.
The liquid medicine is the first original drug to be developed in the past few years by a Hungarian pharmaceuticals company and is aimed at treating sores and wounds that usually heal slowly.

"According to statistical data one to 1.5 percent of the population suffers from these illnesses, which means an additional 25 percent in costs in addition to the costs of the basic illness," Richter said in a statement.

Richter expects to sell 10,000 to 15,000 units of the new solution in the last quarter of 1996 and has applied for approval of the product in the neighbouring countries, Beata Furka, head of market intelligence, said.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Richter shares closed at 8,450 forints, up 200.
